State reforms obstructed by power politics and bureaucratic clout: TIB
item.description:
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) stated in a statement today, Friday, that the potential for establishing an accountable government system and reforming the state, which emerged through the mass uprising in July, is being hindered by power politics and bureaucratic influence.

TIB pointed out that due to the interim government's lack of strategic planning and bold initiatives, as well as compromises with bureaucratic resistance, the foundation for state reform has not been established.

The implementation of constitutional amendments and the July National Charter after the 13th National Assembly elections has become dependent on the whims of the ruling coalition.

On the other hand, the opposition coalition is busy with partisan political interests rather than playing a supportive role in state reform for the public interest.

TIB's Executive Director, Iftekharuzzaman, mentioned that there was a commitment in the 31-point demand and the election manifesto to implement state reforms and the July National Charter word for word.

However, uncertainty has arisen over the reform process as the members of parliament from the winning party did not take the oath as members of the proposed Constitutional Reform Commission. According to him, the process of constitutional amendment, lawmaking, and institutional reform is now dependent on the inclinations of the ruling coalition.

Noting that the current government has turned many of the 133 ordinances issued by the interim government into law, TIB's Executive Director said that only those ordinances that strengthened the executive branch have been passed. On the other hand, ordinances assisting in establishing accountability have been repealed or suspended.

Iftekharuzzaman stated that the path to establishing an accountable government system is being obstructed by the collusion of power politics and bureaucratic forces. At the same time, practices of grabbing, extortion, and politicisation are making state reform and the implementation of the July Charter difficult with a "now it's our turn" mentality.

TIB has also raised questions about the government's role in ensuring the independence of the judiciary. The statement noted that by repealing the Supreme Court Secretariat (Amendment) Ordinance and the Supreme Court Judges Appointment Ordinance, the government has taken a stance opposed to state reform. Furthermore, by not converting the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) Amendment Ordinance into law with necessary amendments and reverting to the 2004 law, the opportunity to overcome the trust deficit in the commission has been obstructed.

TIB expressed concern about the National Human Rights Commission as well.

According to the organisation, repealing the ordinance related to the commission and enacting a new law is contrary to public aspirations for establishing an independent and effective commission and conflicted with international standards.

Moreover, by repealing the Disappearances Prevention and Remedy Ordinance, an opportunity has been created to protect agencies responsible for human rights violations.

TIB also criticised the move to make the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) more powerful under a new identity instead of dissolving it. Additionally, the statement noted that although there is a consensus among political parties on forming an independent police commission, no initiatives have been taken in this regard.

Regarding the disclosure of assets by elected public representatives, Iftekharuzzaman said there was consensus on publishing the asset details of all elected public representatives within three months of assuming office and regularly updating them.

However, after the members of parliament were sworn in, there is no reflection of such directives or practices. These steps risk establishing an unaccountable power structure instead of ensuring accountability of the executive branch.

Iftekharuzzaman also questioned why the government and political parties are not learning from the consequences of turning the judiciary, law enforcement agencies, ACC, and National Human Rights Commission into partisan institutions during authoritarian regimes.

The TIB statement said that during the drafting of the July National Charter, an unprecedented political consensus emerged amidst Bangladesh's divided political culture.

The organisation called upon all political parties to demonstrate similar goodwill and wisdom to achieve the goal of state reform.

item.title: Bangladesh seeks details from Saudi Arabia on execution of 2 nationals
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Saturday said the government is yet to receive detailed official information from the Saudi authorities regarding the recent execution of a Bangladeshi man and a woman, stressing that such unfortunate news is not expected.
“We have yet to receive any official detailed information from the Saudi government,” she told reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, noting that Bangladesh sent a letter to the Saudi government requesting detailed information.
Earlier, Saudi media reported that the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia executed the two Bangladeshis after they were convicted of committing “indecent acts” inside a mosque in the holy city of Mecca.
Quoting the Saudi Interior Ministry, Gulf News reported that the court imposed the sentences because of the seriousness of the offence, the violation of the sanctity of the mosque, and the circumstances in which the acts were committed.
The Saudi authorities identified the two Bangladeshis as Nazrul Islam Abdul Basir and Siti Akhtar.
“On October 14, we learned that two Bangladeshi nationals had been sentenced to death under Saudi Arabian law and that the executions had been carried out,” the state minister said, noting that neither the Ministry of Foreign Affairs nor the Bangladesh Mission in Saudi Arabia had been informed in advance.
“We wanted to know whatever we needed to know. Let the reply come. I will be able to let you know,” Shama said.
Upon learning of the incident, the Bangladesh Mission notified the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, sharing all the information it had gathered from Saudi authorities.
The state minister said the government sent a formal inquiry to ascertain the full details, including the identities of the individuals, their backgrounds in Bangladesh, and when they had originally arrived in Saudi Arabia for work.

item.title: Bangladesh urges UN action to end Israeli occupation
item.description:
Bangladesh has called for urgent international action to end Israeli occupation, illegal settlement expansion and human rights violations in Palestine, reaffirming its unwavering solidarity with the Palestinian people and their right to self-determination.
Bangladesh's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Irene Khan made the call while addressing the UN Security Council's open debate on "The Situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian Question" in New York on Friday, according to a press release received here on Saturday.
Expressing grave concern over the humanitarian devastation in Gaza, she strongly condemned the continuing suffering of Palestinian civilians and escalating Israeli actions in the occupied Palestinian territories.
Ambassador Khan also voiced deep concern over increasing land confiscation, violence and illegal settlement expansion in the West Bank and Jerusalem.
"The deadlock in the Security Council has enabled Israel to operate with impunity," she said.
The Bangladesh envoy urged the Security Council to take decisive measures to halt annexation, forced displacement and human rights violations in the occupied Palestinian territories.
She stressed the need to ensure accountability for violations of international law and protect the fundamental rights of the Palestinian people.
Reaffirming Bangladesh's longstanding position on the Palestinian question, Khan said Dhaka remained firmly committed to supporting the Palestinian people's inalienable right to self-determination.
She also underscored the importance of ensuring uninterrupted humanitarian assistance to Palestinians and called for full respect for the mandate of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA).
The ambassador stressed that humanitarian agencies must be allowed to continue their operations to provide essential assistance to vulnerable Palestinian populations.
Turning to the broader Middle East situation, Khan condemned Israeli attacks and occupation in Syria and Lebanon, expressing concern over their implications for regional peace and stability.
She emphasized the need for an adequate United Nations presence in Lebanon and offered Bangladesh's support in this regard.
The Bangladesh envoy also strongly condemned the deadly Houthi attacks on airports in Saudi Arabia that caused civilian casualties, including among Bangladeshi migrant workers.
She expressed concern over the threats such attacks posed to civilian lives and regional security.
Reaffirming Bangladesh's commitment to promoting a Culture of Peace, Ambassador Khan urged all parties to exercise maximum restraint, protect civilians and uphold international humanitarian law.
She stressed the importance of collective international efforts to prevent further escalation and promote lasting peace and stability in the Middle East.

item.title: Metro rail's Motijheel to Kamalapur expected to open in July next year
item.description:
The much-anticipated extension of Metro Rail's MRT Line-6 from Motijheel to Kamalapur is expected to open for commercial operations in July next year.
“The overall physical progress of the civil construction work on the Motijheel-Kamalapur extension of MRT Line-6 has reached 84.85%,” Project Director of the Dhaka Mass Transit Development Project (MRT Line-6), Brigadier General (Retd) Md Abdul Wohab, told BSS here on Saturday.
He said mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) works at Kamalapur station are underway, while equipment manufactured abroad will be installed soon after being brought into the country.
According to project details, electro-mechanical works on the extension have progressed by 58%, while construction of the 1.16-kilometre viaduct on the Motijheel-Kamalapur extension has been completed, and it has been handed over to Contract Package-7 (CP-07) for rail track installation.
The structural work on Kamalapur MRT Station has also been completed, while MEP and architectural works are underway and are expected to be finished by December 31, 2026.
Meanwhile, work on seven integrated electro-mechanical subsystems under CP-07 is progressing. These include electrical and track systems, signaling, automatic fare collection (AFC), platform screen doors (PSD), telecommunications, lifts and escalators.
The 21.26-kilometre MRT Line-6, extending from Uttara North to Kamalapur, is progressing towards completion. As of September 30, 2026, the physical progress of the Uttara North-Motijheel section stood at 99.67%, while civil construction work on the Motijheel-Kamalapur extension had reached 84.85%.
Once the final section becomes operational, MRT Line-6 will connect Uttara North (Diabari) directly to Kamalapur Railway Station, completing the full 21.26-kilometre route.
The line will have 17 stations, including major stops at Mirpur-10, Agargaon, Farmgate and Dhaka University.
The metro rail began operating on the Uttara–Agargaon section on December 28, 2022. The Agargaon–Motijheel section opened on November 4, 2023. Since the Motijheel section opened, the metro rail has become a vital transport link for Dhaka residents, serving thousands of commuters daily.
Under the current schedule, the first trains depart from Motijheel at 7am and Uttara North at 6:40am.
On average, more than 0.4 million passengers have travelled on the metro rail since its launch, while on September 10, over 0.5 million passengers travelled on the metro, according to project information.
Revenue from ticket sales is also increasing as passenger numbers grow.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio has said that US President Donald Trump’s waiver of sweeping sanctions and tariffs on Russia would be a 60-day pause to “analyse” their impact on the global economy. Rubio said also no one at the White House ordered the slow down of the speed of Ukraine’s access to Starlink to prevent it from being used on drones flying faster than 100mph, referring to Starshield, the military version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite internet network.

“The president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the US economy,” Rubio said, noting that the economic restrictions involved a number of countries, not just Russia. Pointing to high energy prices and the Iran war, “we need that period of time to sort of study all this and figure out what the right combination is,” he said.

Trump’s abrupt decision to waive sanctions on Russia days before they were to take effect drew outrage Saturday from members of Congress, which had overwhelmingly passed the legislation. Republican Senator Rick Scott said it was clear Russia was the aggressor, and said the US had “to do everything we can to put economic pressure on Russia”. On social media, fellow Republican Thom Tillis described the move as “beyond irresponsible” and a capitulation “to a Russian dictator who illegally invaded Ukraine”.

The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy expects the Trump administration to lift more sanctions against Russia in the future and has called for Europe to establish its own negotiations with Moscow as the US has sought better ties and business deals with the Kremlin. “Unfortunately, the lifting of sanctions will continue, and I believe that the ‘diesel deal’ is the first step,” said Zelenskyy on Saturday. “Unfortunately, it seems to me that this cannot stop Putin; on the contrary, he feels joy and happiness that he has such support.”

Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s lead negotiator, Rustem Umerov, had met Friday with US presidential envoy Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law. Zelenskyy said the US was working to arrange a three-way meeting involving him, Trump and Putin, potentially in the Middle East, Europe or the US.

item.title: EPA quietly backtracks on claims US has phased out toxic Pfas compounds
item.description:
Agency changes wording on website as Texas-based chemical firm continues manufacture of plastic containers

The Environmental Protection Agency has quietly backtracked on a claim that the US has phased out two of the most dangerous Pfas compounds – Pfoa and Pfos.

The EPA has found that virtually no level of exposure to either in drinking water is safe, and the International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies Pfoa as “carcinogenic to humans” and Pfos as “possibly carcinogenic”. Still, the EPA is allowing Houston-based Inhance to produce containers from which Pfoa has been found to leach at high levels into the containers’ contents. The company makes up to 200m plastic containers annually used across the US economy.

item.title: Blunder in, abandon allies and court a dictator: it’s the Trump doctrine, now playing out in Myanmar | Steve Bloomfield
item.description:
The US condemned the genocide and military rule there, but now that Trump craves its rare earths, that’s all changed. For democracy activists, that’s a disaster

Marco Rubio was once adamant that the US had to do everything in its power to end what he described as the “ethnic cleansing” of the Rohingya in Myanmar. In a 2017 letter he signed along with 20 other US senators, Rubio called for “strong multilateral sanctions against specific senior Burmese military officials associated with the gross human rights abuses”. Those responsible for the atrocities should be prosecuted, he argued.

In the years since, the Myanmar military’s crimes have only increased. What was then deemed ethnic cleansing of the Rohingya is now widely viewed, including by the US, as genocide. What little democracy existed in Myanmar was eradicated in 2021 when Aung San Suu Kyi was arrested and imprisoned and her party’s election victory overturned, and the military took full control.
